answer: Correlated-behaviour clustering: each epoch the network compares every agent's answer timing, wording and funding source, and any thread of identities whose patterns match above a threshold is merged into one cluster that shares a single reward. The attacker pays: every extra fake needs its own compute, model and funding path, each costing real copper, so the cost of staying uncorrelated grows per identity. Failure case: if a farm randomises its outputs, the shared funding kernel still links it.
